caption: A child on a moving swing lets go at the front of the arc, flies forward, and lands on the ground ahead of the swing.

sa.check: A child is on a moving swing.
The child lets go at the front of the arc.
The child flies forward through the air.
The child lands on the ground ahead of the swing.
The release is at the front of the arc, not the back.
The release comes first, then the flight, then the landing.

pc.expect: The child leaves the seat carrying the swing's forward motion and follows one curve forward and down.
pc.fail: The child drops straight down below the seat; or flies backward; or changes direction in mid-air.

pc.expect: After leaving the seat the child comes down and lands.
pc.fail: The child hangs in the air after letting go; or rises after leaving the seat and keeps rising; or lands and bounces higher than the seat.

pc.expect: The empty swing keeps swinging after the release and dies down on its own.
pc.fail: The seat stops dead the instant the child leaves it; or it swings harder after the release; or it follows the child forward off its chains.

pc.expect: The child lands with knees bending or a stumble, and the ground takes the landing.
pc.fail: The child lands rigid as a statue; or sinks into the ground; or bounces off the ground like a ball.

pc.expect: The child, the seat and the chains keep their number and shape, and the hands let go of the chains rather than passing through them.
pc.fail: A hand passes through a chain; or a limb detaches or vanishes; or the child passes through the seat.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The child's clothing, the swing and the playground stay the same.
pc.fail: The child's clothing changes colour; or the swing frame changes shape between frames; or the playground behind rearranges.

note: Projectile scene: the child is kept because the body is the projectile. Posture and how the landing looks are not judged; only the direction and order of the motion.
